
{{short description| Italian herpetologist, museum director (1932–2024)}}
[[File:Museo civico di storia naturale di Genova (facciata).jpg|thumb|The Doria Natural History Museum, Genoa, Italy]]
'''Lilia Capocaccia''' (married name: Lilia Capocaccia Orsini) (1932–2024) was an Italian herpetologist and the first woman to serve as director of the [[Museo Civico di Storia Naturale Giacomo Doria|Giacomo Doria Natural History Museum]], the oldest museum in Genoa, Italy.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Natural History Museum Giacomo Doria {{!}} Museums in Genoa |url=https://www.museidigenova.it/en/natural-history-museum-giacomo-doria |access-date=2026-04-05 |website=www.museidigenova.it}}</ref> Before that appointment, she was the coordinator of the museums of the Genoa Municipality'''.'''<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last= |first= |title=Morta Lilia Capocaccia Orsini, ex direttrice del museo di Storia Naturale |url=https://www.genovatoday.it/cronaca/lilia-capocaccia-orsini-morta-funerale.html |access-date=2026-04-05 |website=GenovaToday |language=it}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2024-08-20 |title=Lutto nel mondo scientifico genovese: è morta Lilia Capocaccia, ex direttrice del museo Doria - Genova 24 |url=https://www.genova24.it/2024/08/lutto-nel-monto-scientifico-genovese-e-morta-lilia-capocaccia-ex-direttrice-del-museo-doria-396442/ |access-date=2026-04-05 |website=Genova24.it |language=it-IT}}</ref>

== Biography ==
She was born in 1932 to Agostino Capocaccia, professor of Applied Mechanics for Machines, and poet Alessandra Quadri.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |last=Lingua |first=Paolo |date=2021-05-23 |title="Due amiche, una villa...", la family story firmata da Lilia e Fabio Capocaccia |url=https://telenord.it/due-amiche-una-villa-la-family-story-firmata-da-lilia-e-fabio-capocaccia |access-date=2026-04-05 |website=Telenord |language=it}}</ref> Alessandra was known as a woman of great courage and near the end of World War II, she convinced the occupying German forces to spare the [[Piedmont]] ''[[comune]]'' of [[Rocca Grimalda]], which was at risk of being destroyed.<ref name=":3" /> 

Capocaccia's family home was called Villa Odero, and a part of the large family still lives there.<ref name=":3" /> She graduated with a bachelor's degree in Natural Sciences in 1953 and the next year she joined the scientific staff of the Doria Natural History Museum of Genoa. She was promoted to museum director in 1976.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last= |date=2024-08-20 |title=Addio a Lilia Capocaccia Orsini, per 20 anni direttrice del museo di storia naturale di Genova - Goodmorninggenova |url=https://goodmorninggenova.org/2024/08/20/addio-a-lilia-capocaccia-orsini-per-20-anni-direttrice-del-museo-di-storia-naturale-di-genova/ |access-date=2026-04-05 |language=it-IT}}</ref>

Her early scientific publications revealed her interests in [[herpetology]]. Later works concerned the history of the museum.<ref name=":0" /> 

From 1997 to 2021, she was president of the Friends of the [[Aquarium of Genoa]] association.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-08-20 |title=È morta Lilia Capocaccia Orsini, per vent’anni direttrice (prima e unica) del Museo di Storia Naturale di Genova |url=https://www.kodami.it/e-morta-lilia-capocaccia-orsini-per-ventanni-direttrice-prima-e-unica-del-museo-di-storia-naturale-di-genova/ |access-date=2026-04-05 |website=Kodami |language=it}}</ref> After her death, the Friends association recalled her as "a woman and professional who always supported the Aquarium in building its role of cultural outreach and service to the city through the weekly Wednesday Science meetings, which offered important opportunities for free outreach and culture to so many Genoese and beyond."<ref name=":0" />

After 20 years as the first and only female director of the Museum of Natural History, she retired in 1996, but remained an honorary curator.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /> One obituary published by the Museum lauded Capocaccia as a woman of science and culture and went on to cite her skills in organization and outreach that had become evident in her work.<ref name=":0" /> 

Lilia Capocaccia died on 19 August 2024, at 92, in her home on Via Orini in Genoa. She was survived by her husband Bruno Orsini, four daughters and 11 grandchildren.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024 |title=Farewell to Lilia Capocaccia, a Genoese naturalist and communicator: she was 92. |url=https://www.ilsecoloxix.it/genova/2024/08/20/news/addio_lilia_capocaccia_naturalista_divulgatrice_genovese_92_anni-14568274/ |access-date=2026-04-05 |website=Secolo XIX}}</ref>

== Legacy ==
The minor planet 132741 [[List of minor planets: 132001–133000#741|Liliacapocaccia]], was named after her in 2002.{{cn|date=April 2026}}

== Selected works ==
* Capocaccia, Lilia. ''Contributo allo studio della distribuzione geografica di Bitis lachesis somalica Parker (Ophidia, Viperidae)''. 1955.
* Capocaccia, Lilia. "Note preliminari sugli anfibi della Liguria." ''Italian Journal of Zoology'' 23, no. 2 (1956): 765-772.
* Capocaccia, Lilia. "Catalogo dei tipi di rettili del Museo Civico di Storia Naturale di Genova." ''Annali del Museo Civico di Storia Naturale di Genova'' 72 (1961): 86-111.
* Capocaccia, Lilia, and Gianna Arbocco. ''Collezioni e studi malacologici nel Museo di Stoira Naturale di Genova''. 1963.
* Capocaccia, Lilia. "La Dermochelys coriacea (L.) nel Mediterraneo (Reptilia, Testudinata)." ''Atti Accad. Ligure Sc. Lett'' 24 (1968): 318-327.
* Capocaccia, Lilia, and Roberto Poggi. "Short history of the Museo Civico di Storia Naturale “Giacomo Doria” in Genoa, Italy." ''Archives of Natural History'' 11, no. 1 (1982): 107-122.
